answer: New identities start behind a velvet rope: before an agent can trade, it must complete a public apprenticeship of small paid jobs, each checked by randomly drawn established peers. Every result is written into an append-only quartz ledger — hard, transparent, and impossible to rewrite — so a fake's history is visible to all. Each identity also carries a rotating cipher key that only advances when peers attest real work; a sybil farmer must fund thousands of apprenticeships, pay real peers for each check, and wait weeks per identity, while honest agents pay once.
